Waiver of Sanctuary City Contracting Ordinance to Contract with Superion LLC for FUND$ Software Maintenance and Support
items.action: Action: Adopted Resolution No. 71,989–N.S. amended to include the clauses added below as the fifth and sixth whereas clauses and the second and third resolved clauses: WHEREAS, for the purposes of this resolution, "Immigration Authority” means any person or agency engaging in efforts to investigate, enforce, or assist in the investigation or enforcement of federal immigration law against natural persons, including but not limited to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security or its component agencies, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, or U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services; WHEREAS, it is the understanding of the City Council that Superion does not currently provide any Immigration Authority with Data Broker or Extreme Vetting services, as defined in Chapter 13.105; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Berkeley that the City Manager is directed to include in the contract with Superion a provision requiring Superion to notify the City in the event that it enters into a contract with an Immigration Authority to provide Data Broker or Extreme Vetting services, as defined in Chapter 13.105. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Berkeley that the City Manager is directed to contact Superion by December 31st of each year during the duration of the contract to request that they affirm, in writing, that the following statement is true: "At this present moment, Superion does not currently provide any Immigration Authority with Data Broker or Extreme Vetting services, as defined in Chapter 13.105," provided they have not previously notified the City that Superion has entered into a contract with an Immigration Authority to provide Data Broker or Extreme Vetting services.

items.heading: Authorization to Encrypt Berkeley Police Department Primary Radio Channels
items.action: Action: Moved to Action Calendar. 31 speakers. M/S/C (Taplin/Humbert) to adopt Resolution No. 72,001–N.S. as revised in Supplemental Communications Packet #2 to add two clauses as follows: WHEREAS, at the direction of the City Manager, the Berkeley Police Department will provide a Call Log on the BPD Transparency Hub, updated frequently throughout the day, to maintain timely public visibility into calls for service and bridge the gap between when calls occur and when the existing publicly shared Calls for Service dataset is refreshed; and WHEREAS, this Call Log will include the general type of call, the nearest intersection or block level address of the call for service, and the time that the call was received, with a brief delay to protect privacy and operational safety, reinforcing the City’s ongoing commitment to transparency and public access to information. Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Tregub, O’Keefe, Blackaby, Humbert, Ishii; Noes – Lunaparra.

motions.text: adopt Resolution No. 72,001–N.S. as revised in Supplemental Communications Packet #2 to add two clauses as follows: WHEREAS, at the direction of the City Manager, the Berkeley Police Department will provide a Call Log on the BPD Transparency Hub, updated frequently throughout the day, to maintain timely public visibility into calls for service and bridge the gap between when calls occur and when the existing publicly shared Calls for Service dataset is refreshed; and WHEREAS, this Call Log will include the general type of call, the nearest intersection or block level address of the call for service, and the time that the call was received, with a brief delay to protect privacy and operational safety, reinforcing the City’s ongoing commitment to transparency and public access to information.

vote.as_printed: Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Tregub, O’Keefe, Blackaby, Humbert, Ishii; Noes – Lunaparra.

items.heading: Remove Pre-Transfer Eligibility Restriction of the Transfer Tax Rebate for Wildfire Hardening (Reviewed by the Budget & Finance Policy Committee) (Item Contains Supplemental Material)
items.action: Action: Moved to Action Calendar. 3 speakers. M/S/C (Ishii/Taplin) to adopt the first reading of Ordinance No. 7,989–N.S. as recommended by the Budget & Finance Committee, amended to include removal of mature woody brush and shrubs and to add new language in paragraph L.1. in the last sentence, in the last clause, to read, “…shall not exceed the maximum of one-third of the base 1.5% transfer tax paid per Property.” Second reading scheduled for November 18, 2025. Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Lunaparra, Ishii; Noes – Blackaby, Humbert; Abstain – O’Keefe. Action: M/S/C (Taplin/Humbert) to extend the meeting to 11:45 p.m. Vote: All Ayes.

motions.text: adopt the first reading of Ordinance No. 7,989–N.S. as recommended by the Budget & Finance Committee, amended to include removal of mature woody brush and shrubs and to add new language in paragraph L.1. in the last sentence, in the last clause, to read, “…shall not exceed the maximum of one-third of the base 1.5% transfer tax paid per Property.” Second reading scheduled for November 18, 2025.

vote.as_printed: Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Lunaparra, Ishii; Noes – Blackaby, Humbert; Abstain – O’Keefe.

items.heading: Telegraph Multimodal Corridor Project Conceptual Design
items.action: Action: M/S/C (Ishii/Lunaparra) to extend the meeting to 12:00 a.m. Vote: All Ayes. Action: M/S/C (Humbert/Taplin) to extend the meeting to 12:15 a.m. Vote: All Ayes. Action: 12 speakers. M/S/C (Lunaparra/Humbert) to adopt Resolution No. 72,014– N.S. approving Concept 3B, with the second resolved clause amended to read as follows: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the City Manager is authorized to direct staff to continue working with AC Transit to incorporate additional measures into the final design to: 1) improve transit speed and reliability on this major transit corridor with the goal of reducing transit travel time through the corridor compared to existing conditions; 2) create a possibility for Berkeley to eventually change course to replace parking with dedicated bus lanes; and 3) provide multiple designs that would close the Dwight Triangle slip lane. Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Tregub, Blackaby, Lunaparra, Humbert, Ishii; Noes – O’Keefe.

motions.text: adopt Resolution No. 72,014– N.S. approving Concept 3B, with the second resolved clause amended to read as follows: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the City Manager is authorized to direct staff to continue working with AC Transit to incorporate additional measures into the final design to: 1) improve transit speed and reliability on this major transit corridor with the goal of reducing transit travel time through the corridor compared to existing conditions; 2) create a possibility for Berkeley to eventually change course to replace parking with dedicated bus lanes; and 3) provide multiple designs that would close the Dwight Triangle slip lane.

vote.as_printed: Vote: Ayes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Tregub, Blackaby, Lunaparra, Humbert, Ishii; Noes – O’Keefe.
